hints.content:
###Graphing the first point

To graph a line, we need to find two points that are on it. Then we can drag the movable points to those points.

We already have one point, $(-3,-4)$, and we can use the slope of the line to find another point.

[[☃ image 1]]

options.alt: A coordinate plane. The x- and y-axes each scale by one. The point negative three, negative four is plotted and labeled.

hints.content:
###Use the slope to graph another point

We want the slope to be $-5$:

$\text{slope}=\dfrac{\purpleD{\text{rise}}}{\maroonD{\text{run}}}=\dfrac{\purpleD{\Delta y}}{\maroonD{\Delta x}}=\dfrac{\purpleD{-5}}{\maroonD{1}}=\dfrac{\purpleD{5}}{\maroonD{-1}}$

Starting at $(-3,-4)$, we don't have room on the given grid to go $5$ units down and $1$ unit right. So let's go $\purpleD{5\text{ units up}}$ and $\maroonD{1\text{ unit to the left}}$ to plot another point on the line:

[[☃ image 1]]

options.alt: A coordinate plane. The x- and y-axes each scale by one. The points negative three, negative four and negative four, one are plotted and labeled. There is a vertical dotted segment from negative three, negative four to negative three, one that is labeled five. There is a horizontal dotted segment from negative three, one to negative four, one that is labeled negative one.

question.content:
**Graph a line with a slope of $-5$ that contains the point $(-3,-4)$.**
